output.title: Aerobic Base Run with Flat Neuromuscular Surges
output.description: Process: Warm up 15 min easy continuous running @ Zone 1-2 → 30 min steady aerobic running @ Zone 2 (145-152 bpm) → 6 x 15s flat maximum turnover neuromuscular surges with 45s easy walking recovery → Cool down 4 min easy jog. Overall: Initial session of the training cycle establishing baseline aerobic stimulus and neuromuscular motor unit recruitment without structural fatigue. Serves as flat-ground turnover maintenance while strictly honoring environmental constraints. Reason: Scheduled on day one to re-engage mechanical rhythm and assess aerobic status below AeT without cardiovascular or orthopedic strain. Benefit: Stimulates mitochondrial density and enhances fast-twitch fiber recruitment without lactate accumulation or central nervous system exhaustion. Warning: Keep surges snappy but relaxed; do not strain or tie up mechanically, and terminate immediately if hamstring or calf tightness presents.
output.fueling_tip: Sessions < 75 mins: Plain water and optional electrolytes (200-400mg sodium); no exogenous carbs needed.

output.title: Muscular Endurance Foundation Circuit
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min dynamic mobility and light joint activation → 10 reps Split Jump Squats, 15s transition → 10 reps Squat Jumps, 15s transition → 10 reps/leg Box Step-Ups at 75% kneecap height, 15s transition → 10 reps/leg Front Lunges → Perform 6 total rounds with 60s rest between rounds → Cool down 6 min light mobility and lower body stretching. Overall: A bodyweight-only muscular endurance circuit tailored specifically for extreme vertical hiking fatigue resistance in a flat training environment. Focuses on local muscular burn in the quadriceps and glutes while keeping systemic heart rate strictly within aerobic bounds. Reason: Scheduled early in this 10-week shortened runway to bypass general gym strength and immediately initiate vertical chassis conditioning. Benefit: Promotes fast-twitch oxidative adaptations (FTa recruitment) and muscular fatigue resistance necessary for 1000m D+ ascent. Warning: Maintain pristine spinal and knee tracking; ensure heart rate does not spike into Zone 3 or 4, keeping the effort purely muscular rather than cardiovascular.
output.fueling_tip: Sessions < 75 mins: Plain water and optional electrolytes (200-400mg sodium); no exogenous carbs needed.

output.title: Aerobic Recovery Flush Run
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min gentle shuffling jog @ low Zone 1 → 25 min relaxed continuous aerobic running strictly below 135 bpm → Cool down 10 min easy walking and mobility drills. Overall: A low-stress recovery session designed to stimulate circulation and promote structural recovery between intense muscular endurance and weekend aerobic volume. Strictly controlled below aerobic threshold. Reason: Placed after Thursday's muscular endurance stimulus to clear local waste metabolites and reinforce capillary bed perfusion without lingering fatigue. Benefit: Accelerates soft tissue remodeling and enhances parasympathetic tone without depleting glycogen stores. Warning: Do not chase pace; monitor heart rate continuously to ensure cardiac output stays completely within Zone 1 recovery parameters.
output.fueling_tip: Sessions < 75 mins: Plain water and optional electrolytes (200-400mg sodium); no exogenous carbs needed.

output.title: Aerobic Aerobic Base Volume Run
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy jog @ Zone 1 → 40 min steady aerobic distance running @ Zone 2 (145-152 bpm) → Cool down 10 min light jog and gentle hip opener mobility. Overall: Continuous steady-state aerobic run serving as core volume building on flat terrain while reinforcing efficient biomechanics. Reason: Positioned as the penultimate session of Week 1 to develop fat oxidation capacity ahead of Sunday's extended base run. Benefit: Expands capillary beds, enhances stroke volume, and increases mitochondrial density in slow-twitch locomotor fibers. Warning: Keep effort strictly disciplined on slight headwind sections to prevent unintentional threshold creep.
output.fueling_tip: Sessions < 75 mins: Plain water and optional electrolytes (200-400mg sodium); no exogenous carbs needed.

output.title: Endurance Long Run with Post-Run Eccentric Conditioning
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min progressive jog from Zone 1 to Zone 2 → 55 min sustained aerobic running strictly in Zone 2 below AeT (145-153 bpm) → Bodyweight Eccentric Step-Downs: 3x10 each leg off a standard stair, 60s rest → Cool down 5 min walking and lower body flexibility stretches. Overall: Foundational aerobic long run paired with targeted eccentric single-leg step-downs to build knee joint resiliency in the absence of downhill mountain terrain. Reason: Provides the primary aerobic volume stimulus of the week while initiating eccentric patellar tendon loading for steep race resilience. Benefit: Enhances lipid metabolism, improves glycogen-sparing capacity, and strengthens quadriceps tendon elasticity. Warning: Step-downs must be performed with complete control and slow descent; cease eccentric work if patellar tendon irritation occurs.
output.fueling_tip: Sessions 75-150 mins: 30-60g carbohydrates per hour + 300-500mg sodium/hr with 400-600ml water/hr.
